title: Cancellations, doctors' assurances and friends lost to Covid
summary: Promoters cancelled the gigs; doctors on TV downplayed the virus, but he has since lost several friends, including Bucky and Ruth.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Okay. I’m curious, you said you were on tour in Europe. Did you find it necessary to cancel gigs yourself so you could get home?

No. I didn’t have to. Just promoters. Even because I’ll say one more time, I was not willing to cancel myself because we still were around so many people including doctors that were saying that this wasn’t a big deal. You know? There were doctors on TV that they were saying that this was just like a common cold or something, not much worse than a seasonal — and so we listened to that and I think maybe we were hoping that that was the case. But then you know speaking of Facebook, a few days ago it was circulating a post of someone asking if we knew anyone that died with the disease — and I have to say I had quite a few friends and people that I knew that died with the disease. And I had friends that got the disease, some of them went to the hospital and recovered. Some of them they just stayed home. They just had a regular sore throat with a little bit of coughing. A friend of mine just lost the sense of smell for three weeks and that was about the only symptoms. So I have to say probably this is real, because I never had in one certain period of my life four friends dying with the same disease. You know?
And people that meant so much to us, like Bucky and Ruth.
